service.name: Funk band
service.serviceType: Instrumental funk and soul band for parties, after-parties and corporate events
service.description: An instrumental funk and soul band, guitar, bass and drums as a trio or a quartet with a horn or keys, for private parties, company after-parties, summer picnics and retreat evenings across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: What does the funk band play?
faqs.a: Instrumental funk and soul covers: James Brown, The Meters, Stevie Wonder, Herbie Hancock, Sly and the Family Stone, Prince and Earth, Wind and Fire, played by guitar, bass and drums, with a horn or keys at quartet size. There's no singer, so what your guests recognise is the groove rather than the words, and the band can run a set for as long as the floor wants it without anyone waiting for a chorus.

faqs.q: How small can this booking be?
faqs.a: A trio: guitar, bass and drums. It sets up in 12 by 8 feet on one dedicated 20-amp circuit, loads in inside an hour, and plays a dinner set at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table before the night turns.

faqs.q: Will it fill a dance floor?
faqs.a: Yes, at trio size, in a venue where the floor is close to the tables: a private club, a restaurant buyout, a backyard, a company party under two hundred. For a ballroom past that, the quartet with a horn carries better, and the DJ can take the late night on the same sound system when the band is done.

No. This is the instrumental format. When you want the same songwriters sung out front, with a horn on the big choruses, that's the soul and R&B band, which is the sung version of the same idea and books the same way.

Yes, and a patio or a lawn is where a lot of its work is. It needs a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it, and we agree a move-indoors plan with you ahead of time, because a Colorado afternoon turns fast and the electronics stop behaving in the wet.
